name: MD-02
label: Safe D

key_factors: District's 10-point Democratic PVI and strong fundamentals baseline (~22-point margin)
Incumbent Johnny Olszewski running with a $1.0M warhead vs. Wallace's ~$20K raised
No polls or expert ratings, but no evidence of a competitive race
model.rationale: The baseline's Safe D call rests on a solidly Democratic district, incumbency, and a massive financial asymmetry, with prediction markets corroborating at ~94%. Nothing in the dossier suggests movement away from a roughly 20-point Democratic margin.
model.watch: Any late polling showing a single-digit race or unexpected outside spending against Olszewski would warrant revisiting.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Maryland's 2nd District leans Democratic by about 10 points on the partisan index, and first-term incumbent Johnny Olszewski is running for reelection after easily securing his party's nomination. The fundamentals model points to a margin above 20 points once incumbency and the national environment are factored in.

The resource picture is lopsided: Olszewski has raised over $1 million with $614,000 on hand, while Republican Dave Wallace has raised about $20,000 with minimal cash. No outside groups are opposing the incumbent, no general-election polls exist, and prediction markets give Democrats roughly a 94% chance. All available evidence points to a Safe Democratic hold.
